description: Cayu is an open-source Python framework for building and running domain-specific long-horizon agents, with a durable runtime built in.

summary.one_liner: Cayu is an open-source Python framework and runtime for building long-running, domain-specific agents with durable sessions, approvals, spend caps and multi-agent collaboration.
summary.what_it_does: Provides Python APIs for assembling agents from model providers, tools, context and memory, policies, and domain logic, with a runtime that persists sessions, transcripts and checkpoints in SQLite or PostgreSQL so runs survive restarts and redeploys. Tools can be gated by a ToolPolicy that requires human approval before side effects, and budgets (BudgetLimit, BudgetPolicy) are checked before each model call. It includes task workers and scheduling for background or follow-up work, subagents and durable participant requests for multi-agent work, and runners and environments for workspaces and command execution. It also offers a `cayu` CLI with scaffolding (`cayu new`), inspection, checks, evals, guides, and an optional FastAPI server with a packaged Developer dashboard. Claude Code and Codex can be run as Cayu sessions through extras.
use_cases: build a long-running agent that survives restarts
require human approval before an agent acts
schedule background follow-up tasks for an agent
run Claude Code or Codex as a step in an application
scaffold a new Python agent project
run agent-written code in an isolated environment
notable: Durable sessions with ResumeRequest and recovery, configured by ExecutionProfilePolicy on new builds
Approval gating via ToolPolicyDecision.REQUIRE_APPROVAL resolved through cayu.approvals
Spend caps enforced before each model call (BudgetLimit, BudgetPolicy)
Dashboard can be used packaged, ejected as source for customization, or replaced with a custom UI over the control-plane API
Python-only and not a graph DSL: agents, tools and workflows are ordinary Python
caveats: Native Python tools run in the trusted application process; ToolPolicy controls invocation but does not sandbox them, and LocalRunner/DockerRunner are not hostile-code sandboxes
SQLite suits local or single-writer use; sustained multi-process concurrency needs PostgreSQL or another shared store
Cayu Cloud is currently invite-only and optional; the experimental OpenAI subscription provider is for local development only
keywords: build an ai agent in python
